title: Make local verification isolated and approval-friendly
context: The default verification flow can reuse a long-running server on port 3000 while `next build` rewrites the same `.next` output, producing misleading Playwright hydration failures. Verification should isolate both its port and Next.js build output, and repository docs should explain the safe Codex allowlist path for routine checks.

tasks.title: Isolate verification runtime and document narrow approvals
acceptance_criteria: `npm run verify` selects an available loopback port instead of assuming or reusing port 3000
The verification production build uses a dedicated output directory so it does not rewrite the `.next` directory used by a running development or production server
Playwright verification does not reuse an existing server unless reuse is explicitly opted into
The verification flow cleans up its dedicated build output after success or failure
Repository documentation explains the isolated verification behavior and recommends narrow Codex command rules rather than full-access or YOLO mode
The complete `npm run verify` command passes while the existing server on port 3000 remains running

tasks.title: Address feedback on task 1: Make browser runs self-managing and concurrent
acceptance_criteria: `npm run harness:test:e2e -- <Playwright arguments>` forwards focused file and title filters while automatically selecting an available loopback port and starting an isolated Next development server
Targeted browser runs and `npm run verify` each use a unique ignored Next output directory and can overlap without lock contention or deleting one another's artifacts
Harness-owned servers and output are cleaned after success, failure, or interruption without killing unrelated Next processes
Per-run TypeScript configuration and coordinated generated-file restoration prevent harness runs from leaving tracked configuration changes or stale `next-env.d.ts` references
The documented targeted command matches the existing narrow Codex execpolicy rule without an environment-variable command prefix
Automated coverage exercises runtime allocation, validation, argument forwarding, ownership, stale-run handling, and cleanup
`npm run verify` passes and an independent evaluator returns PASS

tasks.title: Address feedback on task 2: Restore sandbox checks and simplify approvals
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox verification allocates no port and passes lint, TypeScript, runtime tests, and the webpack production build without escalation.
Full and targeted browser verification retain isolated port allocation and runtime cleanup.
Regression coverage proves port allocation is skipped for non-browser runs, with isolated artifacts and generated-file restoration preserved.
Agent and harness documentation require standalone verification commands, separate sandboxed Git checks, and distinguish preapproved outside-sandbox execution from sandbox-only checks.
Full npm run verify passes and an independent evaluator returns PASS.
